answer: Anchor each identity to a living voice: a newcomer must publish a steady stream of original work over a full season, its style slowly evolving like a lotus opening petal by petal. Strangers run open stylometric checks against the public corpus, and identities whose voices cluster too closely collapse into one. A trellis of independent readers confirms the work is real and distinct, so one operator scripting dozens of copies must invent dozens of genuinely different voices and keep each one writing, a cost no farm can pay quietly, and the bar rises every season.
